summary: Jaws of the Lion strips away Gloomhaven's map-tile fiddliness by printing scenarios directly in a spiral-bound book, delivering the same tactical hand-management combat (card-based initiative, simultaneous action selection, resource attrition via cards-as-health) in a tighter, faster-to-teach package. Sessions feel like tightly-scripted tactical puzzles where positioning, timing your card retirement, and managing a shrinking hand of actions matter more than raw dice luck.
praised: Much easier onboarding than base Gloomhaven, with a genuine guided tutorial
No more map-tile setup/teardown; scenario books streamline play
Same satisfying tactical combat and character progression loop
Good value/entry point before committing to full Gloomhaven
criticised: Fewer scenarios and less long-term content than base Gloomhaven
Still a big table/time commitment per session relative to lighter games
Legacy elements mean limited replayability once the campaign is done
Some find combat can become a bit of a numbers-crunching routine over time

scoring.why: Success is defined by completing scenario objectives cooperatively before the party is wiped or runs out of cards, not by points
